language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

Hello, I am John, I am a pirate and sail on "Black Evil". We sail the whole world. So I have seen many different places. I find tectonic plates and volcanos facinating! Tectonic plates are the upper parts of the earth's layers, actually pieces of the lithosphere.
They are 5 to 100 km thick. They float on the mantle like ice cubes! Let's explore this some more together!
John is very good with tectonic plates. What do you know about the tectonic plates?

Tectonic plates have different boundaries. Some plates move away from each other. These have a so called "divergent boundary".
Others move closer together and are called "Convergent boundaries".
Then there is a transform plate boundary. Here the two plates move along each other.
Do you know which sort of boundary is present between the two tectonic plates? Choose the correct answer.

On the edge of the tectonic plates there are earthquakes happening more often than anywhere else. Rocks are pushed together and when they break, seismic waves appear. They make the ground shake, cause landslides and mudflows. Buildings can collapse, tsunamis can appear.

The strength of an earthquake is measured with a seismograph. It measures the strength of the seismic waves on a scale of Richter. You need three of these scales to discover the epicentre of the earthquake, which is where the earthquake started.
Let's see how much you know about earthquakes.

Do you know that there are different types of volcanoes? Some volcanoes are formed on the convergent boundaries, some on the divergent boundaries. There are also volcanoes far from the boundaries, they are formed above "hot spots".
A hot spot is formed where very hot mantle material is rising to the surface. When the hot material reaches the top of the mantle magma forms due to decompression melting.
A small volcanic region is the result. These can also just appear in the middle of a plate, for example in the middle of the Pacific plate, the Kilauea volcano on Hawaii.
A volcano can erupt violently or quietly. If the magma has a lot of gases, the gases will erupt suddenly when the magma is near the surface, causing an explosive eruption.
The viscosity of the magma depends on the temperature and chemical composition. When the temperature is high the viscosity is lower.

You can see the change of the viscosity during an eruption. When the lava leaves the volcano the viscosity is low and the flow is rapid. When the lava starts to cool the viscosity increases and the flow of the lava will reduce until it stops.
